plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid regardless of how high I bid above my value, and bidding above my value only risks winning when I'd have negative profit. Bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid equals my private value of $9.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding my true value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses when I shouldn't win. Bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no history to adjust against, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction, where the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding exactly $20 ensures that if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (which will be less than my value, guaranteeing non-negative profit), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me, which is the correct outcome. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities.
